text.tspan: Page 15, A map is a graph with positions
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
THE WEBSITE HOLDS WHAT THE PAGE CANNOT
“see article and entire section in
graphs.sgit.ai about "thinking in graphs"”
Draw on the article and the whole section on thinking in
graphs at graphs.sgit.ai.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“reader doesn't know about this book”
'The graphs book has a line' assumes the reader knows the
graphs book.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“harsh [over: for you too]”
'If you are my age and twenty years inside a field, that
line is for you too' is harsh.
SHOW THE BOOK, DO NOT LIST IT
“we need to show lots of examples here”
Show a graph of a field in someone's head, with lots of
examples.
FACT OR OPINION, VISIBLY
“also show here why some of the biggest
companies in the world are based on graphs”
Show why some of the biggest companies in the world are
built on graphs.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“we need to qualify this better [over: A map
is a graph with positions]”
'A map is a graph with positions' needs qualifying.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“reader has no idea what a Wardley map is
(by page 15)”
By page 15 the reader has not met a Wardley map.
TOPICS FIRST, DETAILS UNDER THEM
“not relevant to the reader”
The shifts in Dinis's talk on Wardley maps are not for the
reader.
DRAW IT
“show this visually”
Draw a Wardley map as a graph with two axes.
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“[struck: The 2018 book said the same thing
from the other side, / That chapter was
about]”
Trim the 2018 framing.
DRAW IT
“yes, and show example [and] visualise this”
'Decisions based on shadows of reality' is right: show an
example, and draw it.
ANSWERS TO FOR DINIS
“First we need to show the Wardley maps &
how to read them → then go into graphs”
The answer to For Dinis: Wardley maps first, and how to
read them; then graphs.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“weird [over: and that I now cannot unsee]”
'That I now cannot unsee' sounds odd.
SHOW THE BOOK, DO NOT LIST IT
“First show example → reality, systems,
nature”
Graphs nest: show it first, in reality, in systems and in
nature, then say it.
